# Cully 0.24.0

- **Private memory for Solo and individual contributors.** `cully setup --all` uses one local owner. Contributors can connect to an existing OAuth deployment with `cully setup --mcp-url URL`, sharing Cully, PostgreSQL, Mem0 and embedding infrastructure. Solo and IC are high-level usage descriptions; there is no mode flag. The service assigns ownership from verified sign-in. Each signed-in contributor keeps private records; sharing and Team project management remain deferred.
- **A smaller memory contract.** Remove guessed project/repository identity, sections, categories, themes and tags. Keep authenticated ownership, the authoring agent, session IDs, task links, timestamps and useful task notes. Sessions now accept the native agent session ID. Retrieval evaluations isolate their data with session references instead of invented GitHub projects.
- **Plug in provider configuration.** Pass `--mcp-auth-config-dir` and `--mcp-auth-env` to OAuth setup. Cully mounts provider files read-only, keeps secrets with mcp-auth, remembers input paths, and chooses the latest stable mcp-auth release automatically. An image override is testing-only and is not reused on production reruns. The guides cover Google-only sign-in and link to mcp-auth's provider documentation.
- **Connection state without a memory call.** A working Codex Cully registration wins over an expired duplicate, including across status pages. Failed and inconclusive checks are distinguished from sign-in requirements, retried sooner, and no longer carry a misleading first-call hint. A zero observed call count remains separate from connection status.
- **Advisor notes with a concrete next step.** Selecting a many-searches or focused-check warning prepares a bounded prompt explaining what the active agent should inspect, run and report. Review and submit it yourself. Old token waste stops generating current advice once newer output has moved on; repeated transcript entries do not refresh it.
- **A clearer homepage.** Focus on recovering stalled work, evaluating and improving the harness, and carrying private context across agents. Historical measurement coverage includes supported Codex history, with unavailable measurements labeled.

## Upgrade the private memory services together

Schema version 8 is a breaking contract change. Back up the source database, stop old data-service writers, run the matching `cully-data migrate`, then start matching MCP/data versions. It removes the obsolete metadata columns and `cully_projects` tool while preserving owners, IDs, note content, timestamps and session/task links. An image-only rollback will not restore removed columns; retain the database backup.

Refresh installed integrations with `cully setup` using your existing options. Old clients sending removed fields must be refreshed. The migration queues owner-scoped Mem0 metadata rebuilds; semantic recall can lag while PostgreSQL lookup stays available. See the [memory upgrade guide](https://docs.cully.net/memory#upgrade-the-private-schema).

Update the CLI with `cully update --version v0.24.0` after publication. Service upgrades remain an operator action. The newest mcp-auth release must support the supplied provider configuration; choosing a release automatically does not add unreleased provider features. Cursor historical measurements remain unavailable.
